title: Connect Any Agent to Business Central
summary: The post explains how to connect external AI agents (Claude, Cursor, GitHub Copilot, etc.) to Business Central using the Model Context Protocol (MCP), focusing on a new multiplatform Python-based MCP proxy that enables agents to read and write data in Business Central. It covers setup, usage, and troubleshooting for production agent deployments.
key_points: Agents differ from copilots by running tools in loops and self-deciding which data to query, versus copilots providing deterministic question-answer flows.
Microsoft's BC MCP Server only initially worked with Copilot Studio; the new BcMCPProxy enables other agents like Claude Desktop, VS Code, and Cursor to access Business Central.
A multiplatform Python version of BcMCPProxy simplifies installation (pip install), works cross-platform on Mac, Windows, and Linux, and integrates better with IDEs than the .NET version.
Setup requires Azure AD App Registration with specific permissions, device-code login, and configuration file generation for different MCP clients.
Common issues include aggressive top parameter limits on results and 401/400 errors requiring permission verification or endpoint updates; explicit requests help retrieve complete datasets.

quotes.text: Agents can do the same - answer questions or even execute actions. But the flow is non-deterministic.
quotes.why_it_matters: Defines the fundamental distinction between agents and copilots, explaining why agents are transformational for Business Central automation.

quotes.text: Agents run tools in a loop.
quotes.why_it_matters: Encapsulates the core mechanism of how agents work, essential for understanding MCP's role in providing tools.

quotes.text: The agent will understand your request, decide which BC API tools to use, execute the queries, and return results in plain English.
quotes.why_it_matters: Illustrates the end-user benefit of the MCP proxy setup - no code writing required while agents intelligently interact with Business Central data.
